WITH strength_vals AS (
    SELECT ha.hero_id, ha.attribute_value
    FROM hero_attribute ha
    JOIN attribute a ON ha.attribute_id = a.id
    WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Strength'
),
percentile AS (
    SELECT MAX(attribute_value) AS thresh
    FROM (
        SELECT attribute_value,
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY attribute_value) AS rn,
               COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
        FROM strength_vals
    )
    WHERE rn > 0.75 * cnt
)
SELECT s.superhero_name
FROM superhero s
JOIN strength_vals sv ON s.id = sv.hero_id
CROSS JOIN percentile p
WHERE sv.attribute_value > p.thresh;

JOIN attribute a ON ha.attribute_id = a.id

    SELECT attribute_value
    FROM (
        SELECT attribute_value,
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY attribute_value) AS row_num,
               COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_count
        FROM hero_attribute
        JOIN attribute ON hero_attribute.attribute_id = attribute.id
        WHERE attribute.attribute_name = 'Strength'
    )
    WHERE row_num = CAST((total_count * 0.75 + 0.5) AS INTEGER)
)

    SELECT ha."attribute_value"
    FROM "hero_attribute" ha
    JOIN "attribute" a ON ha."attribute_id" = a."id"
    WHERE a."attribute_name" = 'Strength'
),
"cnt" AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM "strength_vals"
),
"pct_offset" AS (
    SELECT ((n * 3 + 3) / 4) - 1 AS offset FROM "cnt"
),
"pct75" AS (
    SELECT sv."attribute_value" AS value
    FROM "strength_vals" sv
    ORDER BY sv."attribute_value"

WHERE a."attribute_name" = 'Strength'

questions.nlq: Please provide a list of superhero names together with the name of their publisher and the total number of distinct superpowers each possesses, for those superheroes who have many superpowers.

meanings.hidden_knowledge: The term many superpowers means that the superhero possesses at least four distinct superpowers.
meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT s.superhero_name,
       p.publisher_name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT hp.power_id) AS total_powers
FROM superhero s
JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
JOIN hero_power hp ON s.id = hp.hero_id
GROUP BY s.id, s.superhero_name, p.publisher_name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT hp.power_id) >= 4
ORDER BY s.superhero_name;

    SELECT s.id,
           s.superhero_name,
           ha.attribute_value,
           s.alignment_id
    FROM superhero s
    JOIN hero_attribute ha ON s.id = ha.hero_id
    JOIN attribute a ON ha.attribute_id = a.id
    WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Intelligence'
      AND ha.attribute_value >= 85
)

       sp.power_name,
       al.alignment
FROM intel_heroes ih
JOIN (
    SELECT hero_id, MIN(power_id) AS first_power_id
    FROM hero_power
    GROUP BY hero_id
) hp_min ON ih.id = hp_min.hero_id
JOIN superpower sp ON hp_min.first_power_id = sp.id
JOIN alignment al ON ih.alignment_id = al.id
ORDER BY ih.attribute_value DESC;

questions.nlq: Identify all superheroes displaying exceptional performance across their measured attributes, including their complete name details, primary attribute specialization, and publishing organization.

meanings.hidden_knowledge: The term exceptional means an attribute value that places the superhero in the top 10 percentile when compared to all other superheroes in the database.
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH attr_ranks AS (
    SELECT 
        hero_id,
        attribute_id,
        attribute_value,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY attribute_id ORDER BY attribute_value DESC) as attr_rank,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY attribute_id) as total_per_attr
    FROM hero_attribute
),
top_10_heros AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT hero_id, attribute_id, attribute_value
    FROM attr_ranks
    WHERE attr_rank <= ROUND(total_per_attr * 0.1)
),
hero_best_attr AS (
    SELECT 
        hero_id,
        attribute_id,
        attribute_value
    FROM top_10_heros h1
    WHERE attribute_value = (
        SELECT MAX(attribute_value) 
        FROM top_10_heros h2 
        WHERE h2.hero_id = h1.hero_id
    )
)
SELECT 
    s.full_name,
    a.attribute_name AS primary_specialization,
    p.publisher_name
FROM hero_best_attr hba
INNER JOIN superhero s ON hba.hero_id = s.id
INNER JOIN attribute a ON hba.attribute_id = a.id
INNER JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id;

WITH top_threshold AS (
    SELECT MIN(attribute_value) AS thresh
    FROM (
        SELECT attribute_value
        FROM hero_attribute
        ORDER BY attribute_value DESC
        LIMIT (SELECT CAST(0.1 * COUNT(*) AS INTEGER) FROM hero_attribute)
    )
),
hero_exc AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ha.hero_id
    FROM hero_attribute ha
    CROSS JOIN top_threshold t
    WHERE ha.attribute_value >= t.thresh
),
hero_max AS (
    SELECT ha.hero_id, MAX(ha.attribute_value) AS max_val
    FROM hero_attribute ha
    GROUP BY ha.hero_id
)
SELECT h.full_name,
       h.superhero_name,
       a.attribute_name AS primary_attribute,
       p.publisher_name
FROM superhero h
JOIN publisher p ON h.publisher_id = p.id
JOIN hero_max hm ON h.id = hm.hero_id
JOIN hero_attribute ha ON ha.hero_id = h.id AND ha.attribute_value = hm.max_val
JOIN attribute a ON ha.attribute_id = a.id
JOIN hero_exc he ON h.id = he.hero_id;

WITH percentile_threshold AS (
    SELECT attribute_value
    FROM (
        SELECT attribute_value,
               NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY attribute_value DESC) as percentile_bucket
        FROM hero_attribute
    )
    WHERE percentile_bucket = 1
),
primary_attributes AS (
    SELECT ha.hero_id,
           ha.attribute_id,
           ha.attribute_value,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ha.hero_id ORDER BY ha.attribute_value DESC) as attr_rank
    FROM hero_attribute ha
    WHERE ha.attribute_value IN (SELECT attribute_value FROM percentile_threshold)

WITH intel AS (

           s.superhero_name,
           s.publisher_id,
           ha.attribute_value AS intelligence
    FROM superhero s
    JOIN hero_attribute ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id
    JOIN attribute a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id
    WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Intelligence'
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT i.*,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY publisher_id ORDER BY intelligence) AS rn,
           COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY publisher_id) AS cnt
    FROM intel i

threshold AS (
    SELECT publisher_id,
           MAX(CASE WHEN rn = CEIL(0.9 * cnt) THEN intelligence END) AS p90_intelligence
    FROM ranked

       RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY i.publisher_id ORDER BY i.intelligence DESC) AS intelligence_rank
FROM intel i
JOIN threshold t ON i.publisher_id = t.publisher_id
WHERE i.intelligence > t.p90_intelligence
ORDER BY i.publisher_id, intelligence_rank;

            row_num,
            publisher_total,

        s.superhero_name,
        ha.attribute_value,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ha.attribute_value DESC) as rank_num,
        COUNT(*) OVER () as total_count
    FROM hero_attribute ha
    INNER JOIN superhero s ON ha.hero_id = s.id
)

FROM ranked_attributes
WHERE rank_num <= CAST(CEIL(total_count * 0.1) AS INTEGER)

SELECT p.publisher_name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT ha.hero_id) AS strong_hero_count
FROM hero_attribute ha
JOIN attribute a ON ha.attribute_id = a.id
JOIN superhero s ON ha.hero_id = s.id
JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Strength'
  AND ha.attribute_value >= 85
GROUP BY p.publisher_name
ORDER BY strong_hero_count DESC;

    COUNT(*) AS count
FROM publisher p
JOIN superhero s ON p.id = s.publisher_id
JOIN hero_attribute ha ON s.id = ha.hero_id
JOIN attribute a ON ha.attribute_id = a.id
WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Strength'
    AND ha.attribute_value >= 85
GROUP BY p.id, p.publisher_name
ORDER BY count DESC

       COUNT(DISTINCT s.id) AS strong_hero_count
FROM "superhero" s
JOIN "hero_attribute" ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id
JOIN "attribute" a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id
JOIN "publisher" p ON p.id = s.publisher_id
WHERE a."attribute_name" = 'Strength'

ORDER BY strong_hero_count DESC;

questions.nlq: Hey! Could you help me find the superheroes with high strength? I'd love to see their names and how strong they are.

meanings.hidden_knowledge: The term "high strength" means having an attribute_value greater than 85 for the Strength attribute.
meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT s.superhero_name, ha.attribute_value
FROM superhero AS s
JOIN hero_attribute AS ha ON s.id = ha.hero_id
JOIN attribute AS a ON ha.attribute_id = a.id
WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Strength' AND ha.attribute_value > 85;

meanings.hidden_knowledge: The term "high strength" means being in the top 10 % of Strength attribute values among all superheroes.
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH strength AS (
    SELECT ha.hero_id,
           ha.attribute_value,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ha.attribute_value DESC) AS rn,
           COUNT(*) OVER () AS total
    FROM hero_attribute ha
    WHERE ha.attribute_id = (SELECT id FROM attribute WHERE attribute_name = 'Strength')
)
SELECT s.superhero_name,
       strength.attribute_value AS strength
FROM strength
JOIN superhero s ON s.id = strength.hero_id
WHERE strength.rn <= CAST((strength.total + 9) / 10 AS INTEGER)
ORDER BY strength.attribute_value DESC;

questions.nlq: Hey there! I need you to dig up the superheroes with top tier strength stats. I'm talking about the real powerhouses, you know? List their names, publishers, and power counts. Crucially, I want you to evaluate this status by comparing them against their peers within the same race to keep it fair. Just let me know what you decide defines top tier in that context!

meanings.hidden_knowledge: The term top tier refers to any superhero who is ranked among the top 5 strongest individuals within their specific race category.
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH strength_heroes AS (
    SELECT 
        s.id AS hero_id,
        s.superhero_name,
        p.publisher_name,
        r.race,
        ha.attribute_value AS strength
    FROM superhero s
    JOIN hero_attribute ha ON s.id = ha.hero_id
    JOIN attribute attr ON ha.attribute_id = attr.id
    JOIN race r ON s.race_id = r.id
    JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
    WHERE attr.attribute_name = 'Strength'
),
ranked_heroes AS (
    SELECT 
        hero_id,
        superhero_name,
        publisher_name,
        strength,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY race ORDER BY strength DESC) AS strength_rank
    FROM strength_heroes
),
power_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        hero_id,
        COUNT(power_id) AS power_count
    FROM hero_power
    GROUP BY hero_id
)
SELECT 
    rh.superhero_name,
    rh.publisher_name,
    COALESCE(pc.power_count, 0) AS power_count
FROM ranked_heroes rh
LEFT JOIN power_counts pc ON rh.hero_id = pc.hero_id
WHERE rh.strength_rank <= 5
ORDER BY rh.strength;

meanings.hidden_knowledge: The term top tier refers to any superhero whose strength attribute value places them in the top 10 percentile within their specific race category.
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH hero_strength AS (
    SELECT 
        s.id AS hero_id,
        s.superhero_name,
        p.publisher_name,
        r.race,
        ha.attribute_value AS strength_value
    FROM superhero s
    JOIN hero_attribute ha ON s.id = ha.hero_id
    JOIN attribute attr ON ha.attribute_id = attr.id
    JOIN race r ON s.race_id = r.id
    JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
    WHERE attr.attribute_name = 'Strength'
),
strength_percentiles AS (
    SELECT 
        hero_id,
        superhero_name,
        publisher_name,
        race,
        strength_value,
        PERCENT_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY race ORDER BY strength_value DESC) AS strength_rank
    FROM hero_strength
),
top_tier_heroes AS (
    SELECT 
        hero_id,
        superhero_name,
        publisher_name,
        race
    FROM strength_percentiles
    WHERE strength_rank <= 0.1
)
SELECT 
    t.superhero_name,
    t.publisher_name,
    COUNT(hp.power_id) AS power_count
FROM top_tier_heroes t
LEFT JOIN hero_power hp ON t.hero_id = hp.hero_id
GROUP BY t.hero_id, t.superhero_name, t.publisher_name;

WITH strength AS (
    SELECT
        ha.hero_id,
        ha.attribute_value,
        s.race_id,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.race_id ORDER BY ha.attribute_value DESC) AS rn
    FROM hero_attribute ha
    JOIN attribute a ON ha.attribute_id = a.id
    JOIN superhero s ON ha.hero_id = s.id
    WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Strength'
),
top_heroes AS (
    SELECT hero_id
    FROM strength
    WHERE rn <= 5
)
SELECT
    sh.superhero_name,
    p.publisher_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT hp.power_id) AS power_count
FROM top_heroes th
JOIN superhero sh ON th.hero_id = sh.id
LEFT JOIN publisher p ON sh.publisher_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN hero_power hp ON sh.id = hp.hero_id
GROUP BY sh.id, sh.superhero_name, p.publisher_name
ORDER BY sh.superhero_name;

WITH strength_ranks AS (
    SELECT 
        s.id AS hero_id,
        s.superhero_name,
        p.publisher_name,
        ha.attribute_value AS strength_value,
        s.race_id,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY s.race_id ORDER BY ha.attribute_value DESC) as strength_rank
    FROM superhero s
    JOIN hero_attribute ha ON s.id = ha.hero_id
    JOIN attribute attr ON ha.attribute_id = attr.id
    JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
    WHERE attr.attribute_name = 'Strength'
),
power_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        hero_id,
        COUNT(power_id) AS power_count
    FROM hero_power
    GROUP BY hero_id
)
SELECT 
    sr.superhero_name,
    sr.publisher_name,
    COALESCE(pc.power_count, 0) AS power_count
FROM strength_ranks sr
LEFT JOIN power_counts pc ON sr.hero_id = pc.hero_id
WHERE sr.strength_rank <= 5;

WITH strength AS (
    SELECT s.id AS hero_id,
           s.superhero_name,
           s.race_id,
           ha.attribute_value AS strength_val
    FROM superhero s
    JOIN hero_attribute ha ON s.id = ha.hero_id
    JOIN attribute a ON ha.attribute_id = a.id
    WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Strength'
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT *,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY race_id ORDER BY strength_val DESC) AS strength_rank
    FROM strength
)
SELECT sh.superhero_name,
       p.publisher_name,
       COUNT(hp.power_id) AS power_count
FROM superhero sh
JOIN (SELECT hero_id FROM ranked WHERE strength_rank <= 5) top ON sh.id = top.hero_id
LEFT JOIN publisher p ON sh.publisher_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN hero_power hp ON sh.id = hp.hero_id
GROUP BY sh.id, sh.superhero_name, p.publisher_name;
}

           s.publisher_id,
           s.race_id,

    FROM superhero s
    JOIN hero_attribute ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id
    JOIN attribute a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id
    WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Strength'
)
SELECT st.superhero_name,
       p.publisher_name,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.hero_id = st.hero_id) AS power_count
FROM strength st
LEFT JOIN publisher p ON p.id = st.publisher_id
WHERE st.rn <= ((st.cnt + 9) / 10);

WITH strength_heroes AS (
    SELECT 
        s.id AS hero_id,
        s.superhero_name,
        s.race_id,
        s.publisher_id,
        ha.attribute_value AS strength_value
    FROM superhero s
    JOIN hero_attribute ha ON s.id = ha.hero_id
    JOIN attribute a ON ha.attribute_id = a.id
    WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Strength'
),
ranked_by_race AS (
    SELECT 
        *,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY race_id ORDER BY strength_value DESC) AS strength_rank,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY race_id) AS race_total
    FROM strength_heroes
)
SELECT 
    rb.superhero_name,
    p.publisher_name,
    COUNT(hp.power_id) AS power_count
FROM ranked_by_race rb
JOIN publisher p ON rb.publisher_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN hero_power hp ON rb.hero_id = hp.power_id
WHERE rb.strength_rank <= CAST(rb.race_total * 0.10 AS INTEGER) + 1
GROUP BY rb.hero_id, rb.superhero_name, p.publisher_name

WITH strength_vals AS (
    SELECT
        s.id AS hero_id,
        s.superhero_name,
        p.publisher_name,
        ha.attribute_value AS strength_value,
        r.id AS race_id
    FROM superhero s
    JOIN hero_attribute ha ON s.id = ha.hero_id
    JOIN attribute a ON ha.attribute_id = a.id AND a.attribute_name = 'Strength'
    LEFT JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
    JOIN race r ON s.race_id = r.id
),
tiled AS (
    SELECT
        hero_id,
        superhero_name,
        publisher_name,
        strength_value,
        NTILE(10) OVER (PARTITION BY race_id ORDER BY strength_value ASC) AS tile
    FROM strength_vals
)
SELECT
    t.superhero_name,
    t.publisher_name,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.hero_id = t.hero_id) AS power_count
FROM tiled t
WHERE t.tile = 10;
}

WITH strength_data AS (
    SELECT
        s.superhero_name,
        ha.attribute_value AS strength,
        a.alignment
    FROM "superhero" s
    JOIN "hero_attribute" ha ON s."id" = ha."hero_id"
    JOIN "attribute" att ON ha."attribute_id" = att."id"
    JOIN "alignment" a ON s."alignment_id" = a."id"
    WHERE att."attribute_name" = 'Strength'
      AND ha.attribute_value >= 80
),
avg_strength AS (
    SELECT
        alignment,
        AVG(strength) AS avg_strength
    FROM strength_data
    GROUP BY alignment
)
SELECT
    sd.superhero_name,
    sd.strength,
    sd.alignment,
    (sd.strength - a.avg_strength) AS strength_difference
FROM strength_data sd
JOIN avg_strength a ON sd.alignment = a.alignment
ORDER BY sd.superhero_name;

           ha.attribute_value AS strength_value,
           al.alignment,
           s.alignment_id
    FROM superhero s
    JOIN hero_attribute ha ON s.id = ha.hero_id
    JOIN attribute att ON ha.attribute_id = att.id AND att.attribute_name = 'Strength'
    JOIN alignment al ON s.alignment_id = al.id
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT *,
           PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY strength_value DESC) AS pct_rank,
           AVG(strength_value) OVER (PARTITION BY alignment_id) AS avg_align_strength
    FROM strength
)
SELECT superhero_name,
       strength_value,
       alignment,
       (strength_value - avg_align_strength) AS strength_diff
FROM ranked
WHERE pct_rank <= 0.2
ORDER BY strength_value DESC;

SELECT s.superhero_name
FROM superhero s

WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Strength'

FROM superhero s
JOIN hero_attribute ha ON s.id = ha.hero_id
WHERE ha.attribute_id = (SELECT id FROM attribute WHERE attribute_name='Strength')
  AND ha.attribute_value > 85;

WITH strength_attr AS (
    SELECT ha.hero_id,
           ha.attribute_value,
           NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY ha.attribute_value DESC) AS tile
    FROM hero_attribute ha
    JOIN attribute a ON ha.attribute_id = a.id
    WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Strength'
)
SELECT s.superhero_name
FROM strength_attr sa
JOIN superhero s ON sa.hero_id = s.id
WHERE sa.tile = 1;

WITH strength_ranking AS (
    SELECT 
        ha.hero_id,
        ha.attribute_value,
        NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY ha.attribute_value DESC) AS strength_tile
    FROM hero_attribute ha
    JOIN attribute a ON ha.attribute_id = a.id
    WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Strength'
)
SELECT s.superhero_name
FROM superhero s
JOIN strength_ranking sr ON s.id = sr.hero_id
WHERE sr.strength_tile = 1

WITH strength_vals AS (
    SELECT s."superhero_name", ha."attribute_value",
           NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY ha."attribute_value" ASC) AS ntile
    FROM "superhero" s
    JOIN "hero_attribute" ha ON s."id" = ha."hero_id"
    JOIN "attribute" a ON ha."attribute_id" = a."id"
    WHERE a."attribute_name" = 'Strength'
)
SELECT "superhero_name"
FROM strength_vals
WHERE ntile = 5;

    SELECT id FROM attribute WHERE attribute_name = 'Strength'
),
avg_strength AS (
    SELECT AVG(attribute_value) AS avg_val FROM hero_attribute
    WHERE attribute_id = (SELECT id FROM strength_attr)
),
strong_heroes AS (
    SELECT ha.hero_id
    FROM hero_attribute ha
    JOIN strength_attr sa ON ha.attribute_id = sa.id
    CROSS JOIN avg_strength a
    WHERE ha.attribute_value > a.avg_val
)
SELECT p.publisher_name, COUNT(sh.hero_id) AS superhero_count
FROM publisher p
JOIN superhero s ON s.publisher_id = p.id
JOIN strong_heroes sh ON sh.hero_id = s.id
GROUP BY p.publisher_name;

meanings.gt_sql:
WITH many_heroes AS (
    SELECT hero_id
    FROM hero_power
    GROUP BY hero_id
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT power_id) >= 5
)
SELECT s.superhero_name,
       AVG(ha.attribute_value) AS average_attribute_value
FROM superhero s
JOIN many_heroes mh ON s.id = mh.hero_id
JOIN hero_attribute ha ON s.id = ha.hero_id
GROUP BY s.id, s.superhero_name;

meanings.hidden_knowledge: In this context, "many" means having a number of superpowers greater than the median number of superpowers possessed by all superheroes in the database.
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH hero_counts AS (
        SELECT hp.hero_id, COUNT(*) AS power_cnt
        FROM hero_power hp
        GROUP BY hp.hero_id
    ),
    cnts AS (
        SELECT power_cnt,
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY power_cnt) AS rn,
               COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_cnt
        FROM hero_counts
    ),
    median_val AS (
        SELECT CASE
                   WHEN total_cnt % 2 = 1 THEN
                       (SELECT power_cnt FROM cnts WHERE rn = (total_cnt + 1) / 2)
                   ELSE
                       ((SELECT power_cnt FROM cnts WHERE rn = total_cnt / 2) +
                        (SELECT power_cnt FROM cnts WHERE rn = total_cnt / 2 + 1)) / 2.0
               END AS median_power_cnt
        FROM cnts LIMIT 1
    ),
    heroes_many AS (
        SELECT hc.hero_id, hc.power_cnt
        FROM hero_counts hc
        CROSS JOIN median_val mv
        WHERE hc.power_cnt > mv.median_power_cnt
    )
SELECT s.superhero_name,
       AVG(ha.attribute_value) AS average_attribute_value
FROM heroes_many hm
JOIN superhero s ON s.id = hm.hero_id
LEFT JOIN hero_attribute ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id
GROUP BY s.superhero_name;
